basics.name: Alex Profir
basics.label: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
basics.summary: I like making apps that people are happy to use. I sit down with the client early, so we build what they really need, and most of my apps I've taken from the first commit to release. I like working in a team, remote or hybrid.

work.name: Independent Contractor
work.summary: Since April 2025 I've been working through my own company, on web, mobile and backend, microservices too, all on scalable cloud infrastructure. Clients include MoreDevs, where I stayed on their cybersecurity platform until October 2026, and a faith-based social network, where I'm building their app. I still write a lot of the code myself, but I also lean on spec-driven development and agentic coding. The numbers are in the projects below.

work.name: MoreDevs
work.summary: Client projects. From 2022 my main one was a cybersecurity platform.
highlights: I made cross-platform iOS and Android apps, and user engagement went up
I built responsive web apps in React and TypeScript, and kept maintaining them
I designed and built REST APIs that several services depend on
I took care of website infrastructure, so it stayed fast and reliable
I set up scalable cloud solutions on GCP, AWS and a few proprietary platforms

projects.name: Faith-Based Social Network Mobile App
projects.description: An iOS and Android app for a faith-based social network.
highlights: I'm the technical lead, for a team of 4–6 engineers. Architecture, planning, code review and mentoring, that's my part
I built the feeds and groups, and the video playback. The videos get cached, so you can watch them offline
When a new Expo SDK comes out, I move the app to it
Some things needed native code, so I wrote modules on iOS and Android for audio focus, SMS consent and text input
I set up the CI. It runs linting, type checks, tests and secret scanning, and my Fastlane scripts release to Firebase App Distribution and App Store Connect, so a release is always done the same way
I added Sentry and Crashlytics. We see the crashes and fix them before users need to tell us

I also made a workflow with specs and AI agents. It goes from a Jira ticket and the Figma design to a pull request, and the UI matches Figma. We had features estimated at 2 months or more without AI, now we do them in 2–3 weeks

projects.name: Cybersecurity Mobile Platform
projects.description: A cross-platform product for secure device management and threat detection. It has a mobile app, a web admin UI and a cloud backend. We were 4–6 engineers. I was on it as a MoreDevs employee first, and from April 2025 as a contractor.
highlights: I built the React Native app and the web admin UI end to end
I built threat detection features too, for example catching man-in-the-middle attacks on the device
I wrote two JavaScript SDKs that the mobile app, the web and the backend services use to talk to each other

All the logic was in one monolith, so we started to split it. I built the notification and device management microservices, and the auth one I built with my teammates and kept maintaining, all spec-driven
With spec-driven, agentic development I was shipping features at least 2x faster. That's my team lead's number, not mine
I built integrations with several third-party systems. They send webhooks, and Cloud Run tasks process them reliably in the background
I moved us from Cloud Functions to Cloud Run. The bill went down at least 25% and it scales better
I also did code reviews and performance work, on frontend and backend

projects.name: Guided Tours System
projects.description: A mobile app for creating, searching and managing guided city tours.
highlights: I built the mobile app, where people make tours and search for them
I worked on tour management and the guided flows, on frontend and backend
I added AI-based image moderation, so unsafe images get caught before they go live

projects.name: Job Management App
projects.description: A mobile app for posting jobs and keeping track of them.
highlights: I built the job creation flow: data entry, media uploads, picking the job type
I designed the summary and edit screens
I did the data handling and form validation on mobile

projects.name: Accessibility Management Platform
projects.description: A web platform for managing accessibility.
highlights: I made the layouts work on all screen sizes, and made the frontend faster
There were memory leaks and some inefficient code. I fixed them and the system got more stable
I built a widget that hotels can put on their site to show their accessibility data

projects.name: Video Content Management System
projects.description: A content management platform for video metadata and assets.
highlights: I did the content management on top of a RESTful API
I customized the table components so they fit the design system
I made the frontend more responsive

projects.name: Incident Response and Management System

highlights: I built the user and account management modules
I added live maps where you can see where each vehicle is
I fixed performance bottlenecks and memory leaks in the frontend rendering

projects.name: Sales Management Platform

highlights: I built the admin UI where sales data is managed per organization
I made custom data tables that show the key sales metrics
I made the UI responsive

projects.name: Fitness Administration Platform

highlights: I set up the project and designed its architecture
I did course management on frontend and backend
I worked with the backend engineers to keep the data in sync

projects.name: Art Gallery Management Platform

highlights: I built the admin UI for gallery items and users
I made autocomplete fields that get live data from the backend APIs
I made it easier to move items from one gallery to another

projects.name: Retail Dashboard

highlights: I did analytics pages with live graphs and filters
I added CSV export, so the data can be analyzed and used in reports
I made the dashboard faster, so it handles a lot of data
